problem: A forbid-extra plugin model rejects site-owned YAML variables as plugin Extra inputs.
scope: all plugin configurations, configlib variables, generated schemas and strict run inputs
baseline: The core sends every non-common key into the plugin model and inherits its closed extra policy.
advantages: one core rule covers every plugin
disadvantages: site-key spelling is not generically knowable
defects: third-party models accidentally close the YAML language
bottlenecks: configuration and run-input schemas need different extra policies

metrics.name: schema policy
metrics.threshold: configuration true, plugin fields true, run inputs false

hypotheses: pass the complete resolved tree to expansion

stages.input: declared plugin fields and complete YAML
stages.output: typed declared fields and extensible tree

success_fixtures: plugin tool field validates beside custom keys
rollback: Fix the core boundary; never allowlist one key in one built-in plugin.
stop_conditions: focused and full source tests pass

promotion_decision.reason: configuration extensibility versus input strictness recurs for every plugin

writeback: Document open configuration trees and closed run inputs in project plugin guidance.
